title: Two Friends Debate the Wisdom of Optimizing for a Hundred Years
script: Wisnu: [enthusiastic] I've started fasting on a schedule, tracking my blood markers quarterly, sleeping precisely eight hours. I intend to see a hundred and five, Laras, and I intend to see it well.
Larasati: [amused] That's an admirably specific ambition. Can I ask what you imagine you'll actually be doing with those extra decades?
Wisnu: [defensive] Living them, presumably, with considerably more clarity than most people manage in the decades they've already got.
Larasati: [gentle] I don't doubt the discipline. I question whether longevity, pursued as an end unto itself, quietly displaces the living it was meant to extend.
Wisnu: [challenging] That sounds like the comfortable rationalization of someone who'd rather not confront the discipline required.
Larasati: [wry] Perhaps, though I'd note you've mentioned your blood markers twice already and haven't once mentioned what you actually did yesterday.
Wisnu: [pausing] That's uncomfortably observant. I suppose the tracking has become somewhat consuming, if I'm honest about it.
Larasati: [thoughtful] I'm not arguing against caring for your body. I'm asking whether the vigilance has quietly become the point, rather than remaining a means toward something else entirely.
Wisnu: [honest] I think I'm frightened, underneath the optimization, of an ordinary death arriving before I've actually decided what any of this was for.
Larasati: [understanding] That's a far more interesting confession than the blood markers, and considerably more worth examining.
Wisnu: [reflective] So the tracking is partly a way of postponing that question, deferring meaning by managing metrics instead of actually confronting it.
Larasati: [warmly] That's my suspicion, yes. A hundred and five years spent postponing the question isn't obviously superior to seventy spent having actually answered it.
Wisnu: [considering] I don't think I'm ready to abandon the discipline entirely. But perhaps I'll interrogate why I'm pursuing it quite so anxiously.
Larasati: [encouraging] That seems wiser than either extreme, honestly. Optimize the body, certainly, but don't let the optimizing quietly become the entire life you're optimizing it for.

quiz.question: What has Wisnu started doing to pursue longevity?
options: Taking unproven supplements only
Fasting on a schedule, tracking blood markers quarterly, and sleeping precisely eight hours
Consulting fortune tellers
Avoiding all exercise
quiz.explanation: Wisnu describes fasting on a schedule, quarterly blood marker tracking, and precise sleep as his longevity regimen.

quiz.question: What question does Larasati raise about longevity as a goal?
options: Whether it's medically possible
Whether longevity pursued as an end unto itself quietly displaces the living it was meant to extend
Whether it's too expensive
Whether his doctor approves
quiz.explanation: Larasati questions whether pursuing longevity as an end in itself displaces the actual living it's meant to extend.

quiz.question: What observation does Larasati make about Wisnu's conversation habits?
options: He never discusses health at all
He's mentioned his blood markers twice but hasn't mentioned what he actually did yesterday
He talks only about his job
He avoids discussing the future
quiz.explanation: Larasati points out Wisnu has mentioned blood markers repeatedly but nothing about how he actually spent yesterday.

quiz.question: What fear does Wisnu eventually admit to?
options: Fear of losing his job
Fear of an ordinary death arriving before he's decided what any of this was for
Fear of Larasati's opinion
Fear of failing his blood tests
quiz.explanation: Wisnu admits he fears an ordinary death arriving before he has determined the actual purpose behind his pursuits.

quiz.question: What is Larasati's final suggestion to Wisnu?
options: To abandon all health discipline immediately
To optimize the body but not let optimizing become the entire life being optimized for
To pursue longevity even more aggressively
To stop caring about his health entirely
quiz.explanation: Larasati suggests optimizing the body is fine, but it shouldn't become the entire life being optimized for.
